name: Kled AI
short: A consumer app whose ID-checked contributors capture photos, video and audio to a lab's spec, claimed in under 72 hours.

tasks: custom capture to a spec built from 108 task templates (camera, microphone, screen recording, touch, keyboard)
egocentric hand-task video (e.g. reorganizing a room, two-handed repair)
multi-view object photos (the same object from every angle)
native conversational speech in rare languages

pricing.notes: Not published. The dataset request form asks for a budget band (under $10K, $10K-50K, $50K-250K, $250K+).

latency.typical: Under 72 hours to build and deploy a task to contributors; Kled also says any consumer dataset can be collected in under 72 hours (provider claim)
latency.notes: Kled V3 post, 30 Sep 2026; no SLA. The request form lets the buyer set the date the data is needed by.

freshness.typical_age: Task captures are recorded after the task is deployed
freshness.notes: The catalogue also sells 'Existing files' from contributors' camera rolls; only 'Task capture' (made to order) is a commission.

coverage.notes: Kled says its contributors are 'across the US, Southeast Asia and Europe'. Its Trace ledger, by receipt volume, shows Southeast Asia 74.5%, Sub-Saharan Africa 22.7%, North America 2%, EU 0.4%, MENA 0.3%, Latin America 0.1%. Catalogue task-capture datasets list '100+ countries'. Kled can route contributors to a region (e.g. 'egocentric video from Southeast Asia this week').

licensing.summary: Contributors grant Kled a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide licence, sublicensable through multiple tiers and exclusive to Kled for AI and ML training. Buyers receive 'a license written for model training'; catalogue datasets carry a 'non-exclusive commercial training license' ('train and ship commercial models'), and exclusivity and term are negotiable. The buyer rights come from product-page copy ('Use it to train and ship commercial models'), not a published contract: the Terms of Service contain no buyer licence. The buyer licence text itself is not public; resale, buyer ownership and Kled's own reuse of delivered data are not stated.

human.method: Government ID checked at onboarding; active liveness challenge at every contribution session; each Trace receipt carries the contributor's KYC status (99.9% of receipts from verified contributors).
human.unknown: ID results are not public; only an opaque per-app ID reaches the ledger, and the KYC status on a receipt is Kled's own assertion. The Trace audit page names Didit as the KYC vendor, but no independent audit of the checks is linked.

application.unknown: Task captures are recorded in the Kled app ('Capture Tool: Phone camera (in app)') and the Camera-Original Phone Photos set is 'never imported from a camera roll', but no device or app attestation is published, and the catalogue also contains camera-roll uploads. Capture in the provider's own app or rig is not a server-verified attestation (STANDARD §3).

camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). What is stated: Camera-original files with EXIF kept; terms ban AI-generated content; the FD 1.0 fraud model screens every upload for AI-generated, internet-sourced, edited and duplicate files. FD 1.0 results are from Kled's internal evaluations only; no C2PA signing and no per-file detector result is published.

time.method: Each accepted file gets a Trace receipt within seconds; anyone can look up a file's fingerprint at trace.datafdn.org/verify.
time.unknown: A receipt shows when the file was registered, not when it was captured; which chain anchors Trace is not documented. Trace's integration guide says the on-chain tx_hash stays empty until the DATA Foundation broadcasts, and names no chain, so the anchor cannot yet be checked independently.

location.method: GPS and EXIF are kept in Kled's systems; receipts carry only the contributor's region and GPS existence flags.
location.unknown: GPS values are never public; ledger resolution is 'never finer than country / state'.

content.method: Every submission is scored for task relevance and quality before acceptance, plus consent checks and masking of faces and personal details; task templates include examples of accepted and rejected submissions.
content.unknown: Review criteria and per-dataset rejection data are not published beyond headline QA pass rates.

corroboration.unknown: Nothing independent confirms individual captures; Trace is run by The Data Foundation, which invested $3M in Kled.

custody.method: Each accepted file gets a receipt on The Data Foundation's Trace ledger (content SHA-256 fingerprint, registration time, consent version, KYC status, payout); later changes and revocations append lifecycle events. Anyone can look up a fingerprint at trace.datafdn.org/verify.
custody.unknown: A registration and lifecycle record, not per-hop custody. The on-chain tx_hash stays empty until the DATA Foundation broadcasts and no chain is named, so the anchor cannot be checked independently; Kled's signature on submissions is optional. Trace is run by The Data Foundation, which invested in Kled.

sources.claim: Trace integration: tx_hash empty until broadcast; content SHA-256 is the searchable hash; signatures optional
Every receipt onchain via Trace; revocation appends a lifecycle event

delivery.basis: 'Any consumer dataset that can exist, can now be collected from physical reality in under 72 hours' and 'deployed to 500,000+ contributors within 72 hours' (Kled V3 post, 30 Sep 2026).

auth.how_to_get: Submit a dataset request at kled.ai/datasets or contact sales; customers sign in at the Enterprise Portal (enterprise.kled.ai). Kled says self-serve task design is coming 'soon'.

mcp.notes: No Kled server in the official MCP Registry (searched 'kled', 2026-10-26).

api.notes: No public API docs. Dataset pages offer a 'Copy .md' button that exports specs and licence terms for an AI assistant.

access.notes: Kled's Terms of Service §4.2 ban bots, scrapers and ML training on the consumer Services unless agreed with Kled; buyer work is by agreement, so automation_allowed is left unstated.

payment.notes: No buyer payment method is published; terms are set with sales.

requester.checks: The dataset request form verifies the requester's email with a one-time code and a CAPTCHA.
requester.unknown: Kled publishes no check of who a buyer is or what a commission is for.

attestations.scope: security and privacy audit of Kled
attestations.result: Completed May 2026 (stated on Kled's audit portal; no report published by Trail of Bits)

summary: A consumer app whose 500,000+ opt-in contributors (company figure) capture photos, video and audio to a buyer's spec, built from 108 task templates and claimed in under 72 hours. Contributors are ID-checked via Didit and pass a liveness check each session; uploads are screened by Kled's fraud model, and each accepted file gets a public receipt on the Trace audit ledger (consent version, KYC status, payout). Buyers get a model-training licence. Ordering is through sales; self-serve is announced as coming.

sources.claim: 500,000+ opt-in contributors across the US, SEA and Europe; 108 templates; collection and deployment in under 72 hours; self-serve 'soon'; FD 1.0 fraud model; relevance and quality scoring; regional routing

Custom order flow (spec, contributors capture, QA, consent checks, face masking); delivery with consent records and a licence for model training; request form fields (budget bands, licence type, email verification)
Task-capture dataset: in-app phone camera, non-exclusive commercial training licence, exclusivity negotiable, 100+ countries

Submitted content is licensed or sold to third parties to train AI; KYC uses government ID and biometric data
